name: Fragannot
summary: A proteomics tool that annotates fragment ions in mass spectra, shipped with a graphical interface. It keeps two implementations of the annotation step side by side, a plain Python one and a Codon-jitted one in fragannot_codon.py, so the accelerated path can be swapped in from the GUI.
why_codon: No written claim. Inferred from the parallel Codon-jitted module beside the plain Python one that Codon is the optional accelerator for the annotation loop.

name: KapiBara ROS2 Robot
summary: A ROS2 robot stack. Codon appears inside the mind node, map_mind.py, where the jit decorator is applied to the mapping computation that runs on the robot.
why_codon: No written claim. Inferred from the decorator sitting on the mapping routine inside a ROS2 node that Codon is used to speed up an on-robot compute step.

name: ArquiMundo API
summary: A web API whose single app.py applies the Codon jit decorator to a compute path inside the request handling.
why_codon: No written claim. Inferred from the decorator's placement in the application's compute path.

name: UdemyPythonPro
summary: Course material for an advanced Python course. Codon appears in the CPython chapter as one of the acceleration options taught, with a math.py demonstrating the jit decorator alongside the chapter's other approaches.
why_codon: No claim of its own. Inferred from placement in a chapter comparing CPython acceleration options that Codon is taught as one alternative among several.

name: python-optimizers-demo
summary: A demonstration of Python optimizers compared side by side, with codon_basic.py holding the Codon jit version of the shared example.
why_codon: No written claim. Inferred from the repo's structure, one file per optimizer over the same example, that Codon is one of the compared accelerators.

name: girip11/advent_of_code
summary: Advent of Code solutions in Python, with a codon_impl.py sitting beside the plain main.py for the 2025 day 1 puzzle so the two implementations can be run against each other.
why_codon: No written claim. Inferred from the paired main.py and codon_impl.py for the same puzzle that Codon is being compared against plain Python.

name: CodonNetworkx
summary: An experiment in running NetworkX-style graph work through Codon, with the jit decorator applied in main.py. The name states the intent: NetworkX under Codon.
why_codon: No written claim. Inferred from the repo name and the jit decorator in main.py that the point is testing NetworkX-style graph code under Codon.

name: N-Queens
summary: A long-running collection of N-Queens solvers across many languages and parallelisation strategies, including CUDA. The Codon work lives in .py files, not .codon: a 10Bit_Python/codon directory whose nq.py and parallel.py use the @par decorator and import par and atomic from codon. A second instance of Codon source outside the .codon extension.
why_codon: No claim about Codon specifically. Inferred from a repo whose whole purpose is comparing solver implementations across languages that the Codon directory is one more comparison point.
note: Codon in .py files, found via the codon-import lane rather than extension:codon. See docs/gaps.md. Scale reads zero because the counters key on the .codon extension; the code is real.

name: UnifyWeaver
summary: A Prolog system that compiles logic programs to other languages, with Codon as one of its emission targets. python_codon_target.pl generates Codon-compatible Python, and its header documents what the target can rely on -- native LLVM compilation, the jit decorator for use inside regular Python, GPU support through par -- and what it cannot, namely Python's dynamic features. Codon is a compilation target here, not a dependency.
why_codon: The target file's header states Codon compiles a subset of Python to native code via LLVM and lists near-C++ performance for numerical code as the reason for the target.
note: A code generator that EMITS Codon. Neither an ordinary user nor a compiler plugin; the emitted code lives in generated output, not in the repo.

name: kpu-sim
summary: A functional and transaction-level simulator for the Stillwater KPU accelerator. It carries a design document for integrating Exaloop's Codon compiler with the simulator, but no Codon code: the integration is proposed, not built.
why_codon: A dedicated design document proposes Codon as the front end for the accelerator's programming model.
note: Worth watching rather than counting: an accelerator vendor designing a Codon front end is a different kind of signal from a user, but nothing is implemented yet.

name: agent-engineering-handbook
summary: A handbook of engineering guidance for coding agents. Its Python performance-optimization reference lists Codon among the options an agent may reach for, naming the jit decorator for general Python work alongside NumPy-focused and C-extension alternatives.
why_codon: The reference recommends Codon for performance-critical general Python code.
note: Guidance aimed at coding agents rather than people. A distinct channel by which Codon reaches new code.

name: scientificcoder
summary: A blog-post archive on scientific programming. One post assesses Codon and raises its licence as the obstacle -- not permissive, so commercial production use must be paid for -- and judges it more of a startup product than a community language. The only critical assessment of Codon found in the index.
why_codon: The post discusses Codon's licensing as a barrier to commercial adoption.

name: llmref
summary: A registry of llms.txt reference bundles for many projects, one entry per project per snapshot date. Codon has an entry, so the documentation is packaged for model consumption. Not a user of Codon and not a mirror of its site, but a channel through which Codon's documentation reaches language models.
why_codon: The registry carries a dated Codon bundle among its projects.
